title: Sharpness of the Cyclic Integral Floer Bound Below the Stable Morse Number
coverage: I read all five sections in full: introduction, morse, involution (statements and key steps), geometry and construction. I checked these by hand: the center codimensions against the shift range k=1..L-r, the disjointness of the centers (2·90+3·165+2·495=1665=N+1), the Segre dimensions, and the f_r tables. I also checked the delta pattern and both convolutions, e_C=(1,1) giving no positive entries and e_M=(1,6,1) giving +4 at j=3 and at j=L. A Python script independently recomputed b(X)=174281, lambda(C)=468058, beta_cyc(M)=4·lambda(C)=1872232 and lambda(M)=1872264, so the gap is exactly 32. I checked the bielliptic homology (the Smith normal form of zeta_3-1 is diag(1,3)), the integral blow-up proof, the proof of SM>=lambda (the side boundary has critical values ±T^2 outside the band), and the use of Smale's theorem (dimensions 3330 and 3332 are both at least 6, and both manifolds are simply connected). For the involution and perturbation part and the surface Y with four fixed CP^1, I relied on the companion branches in family 347, which had already verified the same argument.
main_claim: There is a simply connected closed Kähler manifold M = X×Y of complex dimension 1666 with minimal Chern number 1. It carries a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with exactly beta_cyc(M) = 1,872,232 fixed points, all with contractible orbit loops, while SM(M) = lambda(M) = 1,872,264, which is 32 more.
sibling_notes: This paper uses the same skeleton as the companion papers in family 347: the S_2/S_3 bielliptic surfaces, the half-turn on Y with four fixed CP^1, Prop inv:perturb, and Smale's theorem. The only new ingredient is the choice of seven blow-up centers, which makes 4·lambda(C) equal beta_cyc(M) exactly. I verified that arithmetic in full.
